one_month_reasoning: Three scheduled events fall inside the window to 2026-10-30. (1) Microsoft's FQ1 FY27 earnings, expected about Oct 27-28 after the close (date estimated, not yet confirmed; consensus EPS about $4.72-4.82). Last quarter it beat by about 12% ($4.74 vs $4.24) and guided Azure to about 45% cc growth, and demand still exceeds supply. The pattern this year is a strong beat followed by a reaction driven by capex and FCF (the stock fell after Q2 and Q3 FY26 prints despite beats), so the earnings move is roughly symmetric with fat tails. (2) The FOMC meets Oct 27-28. Kalshi and Polymarket price about 56% for a second 25bp hike after the Sept 17 hike to 3.75-4.00%, with CPI at 3.4% and WTI above $100, so the macro tilt is mildly negative for long-duration mega-cap multiples. (3) The Sept jobs report (Oct 2) and CPI (mid-Oct). Short-horizon regularities are post-earnings drift from the July beat and positive momentum (+48% off the June low, a 4% Copilot-driven jump on Sept 25, and +1.8% on Sept 30). Those give a small positive drift offset by the hawkish Fed. Net: median about $520 (+0.4%), and I use roughly 9.5-10% effective one-month vol (slightly above the 32%/3.5 = 9.1% baseline because earnings are in the window) with fat tails.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (Sept-2027 NTM EPS about $22.6 x 25 = $565), a SOTP with the core at 23.5x plus the OpenAI stake at a discount ($560), and a TTM-multiple reversion toward a rate-adjusted 10-year average ($20.7 x 27 = $559). Weighted: $562.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Sept 2027 about $22.6 (0.25 x FY27 $19.76 + 0.75 x FY28 about $23.6) x 25x forward

inputs_detail.derivation: Gurufocus shows forward P/E of 24.7 on Jun-2027 and 20.7 on Jun-2028 at the same price, which implies FY28/FY27 EPS of about 1.19x. Applied to the $19.76 consensus.
One quarter of FY27 plus three quarters of FY28.

The 10-year median TTM P/E is about 32.5 and the average about 31.4, with a range of 21-62. The current TTM P/E is about 28.3 and the forward P/E about 25. I hold it at 25x instead of reverting to the mean because the Fed is hiking again (3.75-4.00%), CPI is 3.4%, and the AI capex cycle keeps depressing FCF conversion.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Core ex-OpenAI: $22.6 NTM EPS x 23.5x = $531; plus the 27% OpenAI stake at about $1T = $270B / 7.45B shares = $36/share, taken at 80% for tax, lock-up and IPO timing = $29

inputs_detail.derivation: The 25x headline multiple less about 1.5 turns, the approximate share of the current valuation attributable to the OpenAI stake (about 7% of market cap).

Polymarket (Sept 8 2026, $233K volume) gives 80% for at least $1.5T and 95% for more than $1T conditional on an IPO by end-2027. I use a conservative $1T because the timing slipped (Altman: no 2026 IPO) and the markets are thin.
Q4 FY26 non-GAAP net income of $35.3B / non-GAAP EPS of $4.74.
IPO timing risk (30% odds of slipping into 2027 were priced in May, and it did slip), plus tax and lock-up.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Historical-multiple reversion: TTM EPS at Sept 2027 about $20.7 (0.75 x $19.76 + 0.25 x $23.6) x 27x (a rate-adjusted discount to the 10-year average TTM P/E of 31.4)

inputs_detail.derivation: Three quarters of FY27 consensus plus one quarter of the FY28 estimate.
The 10-year average is 31.4 and the median 32.5, and the stock trades at 28.3 today. Taking about 15% off the average for higher rates and capex-heavy FCF gives 27x.

bear.story: The AI capex ROI scare returns (the Morgan Stanley-type warning), rates keep rising with oil above $100, OpenAI's IPO slips or prices low, which exposes that about 45% of RPO is concentrated in OpenAI, and the multiple compresses to about 18-19x NTM EPS of $21. This repeats the June 2026 low ($349) and the 2022 drawdown (-37%).

base.story: Azure grows 40%+ as capacity comes online, FY27 EPS of about $19.8 is delivered, and capex growth decelerates with the calendar-2026 capex guide cut to about $175B. The multiple holds near 25x forward, and the OpenAI stake gets marked via an IPO in H1 2027.

bull.story: RPO of $678B converts, Copilot monetizes, and FCF inflects as capex growth slows. An OpenAI IPO at $1.5T or more crystallizes about $50+/share, and the multiple re-rates toward the 10-year average (about 30x forward on $23+ EPS).

thesis_break_reason: Below about $400 (about 18x NTM EPS, below the 10-year P/E floor of about 21 on a TTM basis), the market would be pricing an earnings downgrade rather than multiple noise. Most likely causes: Azure growth decelerating below 30%, OpenAI contract or backlog impairment, or capex that fails to convert to revenue. The June 2026 low of $349 came with Q3 earnings intact, so a revisit of about $400 with estimates cut would mean the fundamental story broke.

reasoning: Base-rate anchor: MSFT's own 1-year realized vol is 32%, and large caps typically move 25-35% a year. Historical MSFT drawdowns average about 17% peak-to-trough with a median recovery of about 4 months (Trefis), but the deep ones (2000 -60%, 2008-09 -58%, 2022 -37%) came in rate or valuation shocks. The stock just went through a -37% AI-capex drawdown (Jul 2025 high $555 to Jun 2026 low $349.20, its worst quarter since 2008 in Q1 2026) and has recovered 48% to $518. That recovery is similar to 2022-23, where the -37% drawdown was fully recovered in about 7.5 months, which argues for continued, but not explosive, upside. Fundamentals are strong: FY26 revenue of $331.8B (+18%), non-GAAP EPS of $17.28 (+22%), Azure +43% guided to 45%, and RPO of $678B. FY27 consensus EPS is $19.76, the analyst mean target $577 across 55 analysts. The multiple is below its history (TTM P/E 28 vs a 10-year median of 32.5). Against that, macro is unusually hostile for duration: the Fed hiked in Sept 2026 and prediction markets give about 56% for another hike in October, CPI is 3.4%, WTI is above $100, and Kalshi gives about 23% for a 2027 recession. My blended fair value of $562 (P/E, SOTP with the OpenAI stake, and historical-multiple reversion) implies about +8%. I set the distribution median at about $548 (+6%, a haircut to fair value for macro and OpenAI-concentration risk) with a lognormal core at 27% vol plus a 20% fat-tail component at 1.6x vol (effective about 31%, in line with the 32% realized). This gives P(at least 518) of about 0.58 and P(at least 700) of about 0.20. Scenarios: bear $380 (25%), base $560 (50%), bull $720 (25%), mean about $555, consistent with the ladder. Research was limited: several sites (CNBC, Kalshi, Polymarket analytics, SEC direct download) blocked or rate-limited fetches, so some prediction-market figures come from secondary reports, with dates as given; the Kalshi 2027-recession probability (about 23%) is from a search summary of the Kalshi page and should be treated as approximate.
